page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor, this instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average tier, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. However, multi-core performance is weak, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2036.0 and a poor stress-ng multi-core rating. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, registering poor results for both read and write operations on large blocks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-highmem-2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core at a lower entry point than larger memory-optimized instances. This makes it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. Tradeoffs include poor database operation performance and weak static web serving throughput, making it less suitable for high-traffic web servers or heavy database engines.

This instance is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive applications, basic text processing, single-threaded scripting tasks, and small-scale caching layers. It can also handle basic, low-throughput LLM inference for small models, though performance degrades significantly on larger models.
